28: 	// lexer is a utility which can get values, token by
29: 	// token, from a Reader. A token is a word, and tokens
30: 	// are separated by whitespace. A word can be enclosed
31: 	// in quotes if it contains whitespace.
32: 	lexer struct {
33: 		reader       *bufio.Reader
34: 		token        Token
35: 		line         int
36: 		skippedLines int
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	// Token represents a single parsable unit.
40: 	Token struct {
41: 		File          string
42: 		imports       []string
43: 		Line          int
44: 		Text          string
45: 		wasQuoted     rune // enclosing quote character, if any
46: 		heredocMarker string
47: 		snippetName   string
48: 	}
49: )
50: 
51: // Tokenize takes bytes as input and lexes it into
52: // a list of tokens that can be parsed as a Caddyfile.
53: // Also takes a filename to fill the token's File as
54: // the source of the tokens, which is important to
55: // determine relative paths for `import` directives.
56: func Tokenize(input []byte, filename string) ([]Token, error) {
57: 	l := lexer{}
58: 	if err := l.load(bytes.NewReader(input)); err != nil {
59: 		return nil, err
60: 	}
61: 	var tokens []Token
62: 	for {
63: 		found, err := l.next()
64: 		if err != nil {
65: 			return nil, err
66: 		}
67: 		if !found {
68: 			break
69: 		}
70: 		l.token.File = filename
71: 		tokens = append(tokens, l.token)
72: 	}
73: 	return tokens, nil
74: }
75: 
76: // load prepares the lexer to scan an input for tokens.
77: // It discards any leading byte order mark.
78: func (l *lexer) load(input io.Reader) error {
79: 	l.reader = bufio.NewReader(input)
80: 	l.line = 1
81: 
82: 	// discard byte order mark, if present
83: 	firstCh, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
84: 	if err != nil {
85: 		return err
86: 	}
87: 	if firstCh != 0xFEFF {
88: 		err := l.reader.UnreadRune()
89: 		if err != nil {
90: 			return err
91: 		}
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	return nil
95: }
96: 
97: // next loads the next token into the lexer.
98: // A token is delimited by whitespace, unless
99: // the token starts with a quotes character (")
100: // in which case the token goes until the closing
101: // quotes (the enclosing quotes are not included).
102: // Inside quoted strings, quotes may be escaped
103: // with a preceding \ character. No other chars
104: // may be escaped. The rest of the line is skipped
105: // if a "#" character is read in. Returns true if
106: // a token was loaded; false otherwise.
107: func (l *lexer) next() (bool, error) {
108: 	var val []rune
109: 	var comment, quoted, btQuoted, inHeredoc, heredocEscaped, escaped bool
110: 	var heredocMarker string
111: 
112: 	makeToken := func(quoted rune) bool {
113: 		completeLexerToken(&l.token, val, quoted, heredocMarker)
114: 		return true
115: 	}
116: 
117: 	for {
118: 		// Read a character in; if err then if we had
119: 		// read some characters, make a token. If we
120: 		// reached EOF, then no more tokens to read.
121: 		// If no EOF, then we had a problem.
122: 		ch, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
123: 		if err != nil {
124: 			if len(val) > 0 {
125: 				if inHeredoc {
126: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("incomplete heredoc <<%s on line #%d, expected ending marker %s", heredocMarker, l.line+l.skippedLines, heredocMarker)
127: 				}
128: 
129: 				return makeToken(0), nil
130: 			}
131: 			if err == io.EOF {
132: 				return false, nil
133: 			}
134: 			return false, err
135: 		}
136: 
137: 		// detect whether we have the start of a heredoc
138: 		if !inHeredoc && !heredocEscaped && len(val) > 1 && string(val[:2]) == "<<" {
139: 			if ch == '<' {
140: 				return false, fmt.Errorf("too many '<' for heredoc on line #%d; only use two, for example <<END", l.line)
141: 			}
142: 			if ch == '\r' {
143: 				continue
144: 			}
145: 			// after hitting a newline, we know that the heredoc marker
146: 			// is the characters after the two << and the newline.
147: 			// we reset the val because the heredoc is syntax we don't
148: 			// want to keep.
149: 			if ch == '\n' {
150: 				heredocMarker = string(val[2:])
151: 				if !heredocMarkerRegexp.Match([]byte(heredocMarker)) {
152: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("heredoc marker on line #%d must contain only alpha-numeric characters, dashes and underscores; got '%s'", l.line, heredocMarker)
153: 				}
154: 
155: 				inHeredoc = true
156: 				l.skippedLines++
157: 				val = nil
158: 				continue
159: 			}
160: 			val = append(val, ch)
161: 			continue
162: 		}
163: 
164: 		// if we're in a heredoc, all characters are read as-is
165: 		if inHeredoc {
166: 			val = append(val, ch)
167: 
168: 			if ch == '\n' {
169: 				l.skippedLines++
170: 			}
171: 
172: 			// check if we're done, i.e. that the last few characters are the marker
173: 			if len(val) > len(heredocMarker) {
174: 				if heredocMarker == string(val[len(val)-len(heredocMarker):]) {
175: 					stringVal := stringifyLexerValue(val)
176: 					lastNewline := strings.LastIndex(stringVal, "\n")
177: 					lines := strings.Split(stringVal[:lastNewline+1], "\n")
178: 					paddingToStrip := stringVal[lastNewline+1 : len(stringVal)-len(heredocMarker)]
179: 					var out string
180: 					heredocLines := lines[:len(lines)-1]
181: 					for lineNum, lineText := range heredocLines {
182: 						index := strings.Index(lineText, paddingToStrip)
183: 						if index != 0 {
184: 							return false, fmt.Errorf("mismatched leading whitespace in heredoc <<%s on line #%d [%s], expected whitespace [%s] to match the closing marker", heredocMarker, l.line+lineNum+1, lineText, paddingToStrip)
185: 						}
186: 						stripped := lineText[len(paddingToStrip):]
187: 						joined := stripped + "\n"
188: 						normalized := stripLexerCarriageReturns(joined)
189: 						out += normalized
190: 					}
191: 					out = strings.TrimSuffix(out, "\n")
192: 					val = []rune(out)
193: 					l.line += l.skippedLines
194: 					l.skippedLines = 0
195: 					return makeToken('<'), nil
196: 				}
197: 			}
198: 
199: 			// stay in the heredoc until we find the ending marker
200: 			continue
201: 		}
202: 
203: 		// track whether we found an escape '\' for the next
204: 		// iteration to be contextually aware
205: 		if lexerStartsEscape(ch, escaped, btQuoted) {
206: 			escaped = true
207: 			continue
208: 		}
209: 
210: 		if lexerIsQuotedMode(quoted, btQuoted) {
211: 			if quoted && escaped {
212: 				// all is literal in quoted area,
213: 				// so only escape quotes
214: 				if ch != '"' {
215: 					val = append(val, '\\')
216: 				}
217: 				escaped = false
218: 			} else {
219: 				if lexerClosesQuoted(ch, quoted, btQuoted) {
220: 					return makeToken(ch), nil
221: 				}
222: 			}
223: 			// allow quoted text to wrap continue on multiple lines
224: 			if ch == '\n' {
225: 				l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
226: 				l.skippedLines = 0
227: 			}
228: 			// collect this character as part of the quoted token
229: 			val = append(val, ch)
230: 			continue
231: 		}
232: 
233: 		if unicode.IsSpace(ch) {
234: 			// ignore CR altogether, we only actually care about LF (\n)
235: 			if ch == '\r' {
236: 				continue
237: 			}
238: 			// end of the line
239: 			if ch == '\n' {
240: 				// newlines can be escaped to chain arguments
241: 				// onto multiple lines; else, increment the line count
242: 				if escaped {
243: 					l.skippedLines++
244: 					escaped = false
245: 				} else {
246: 					l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
247: 					l.skippedLines = 0
248: 				}
249: 				// comments (#) are single-line only
250: 				comment = false
251: 			}
252: 			// any kind of space means we're at the end of this token
253: 			if len(val) > 0 {
254: 				return makeToken(0), nil
255: 			}
256: 			continue
257: 		}
258: 
259: 		// comments must be at the start of a token,
260: 		// in other words, preceded by space or newline
261: 		if lexerStartsComment(ch, len(val)) {
262: 			comment = true
263: 		}
264: 		if comment {
265: 			continue
266: 		}
267: 
268: 		if len(val) == 0 {
269: 			l.token = Token{Line: l.line}
270: 			if ch == '"' {
271: 				quoted = true
272: 				continue
273: 			}
274: 			if ch == '`' {
275: 				btQuoted = true
276: 				continue
277: 			}
278: 		}
279: 
280: 		if escaped {
281: 			// allow escaping the first < to skip the heredoc syntax
282: 			if ch == '<' {
283: 				heredocEscaped = true
284: 			} else {
285: 				val = append(val, '\\')
286: 			}
287: 			escaped = false
288: 		}
289: 
290: 		val = append(val, ch)
291: 	}
292: }
293: 
294: func (t Token) Quoted() bool {
295: 	return t.wasQuoted > 0
296: }
297: 
298: // NumLineBreaks counts how many line breaks are in the token text.
299: func (t Token) NumLineBreaks() int {
300: 	lineBreaks := strings.Count(t.Text, "\n")
301: 	if t.wasQuoted == '<' {
302: 		// heredocs have an extra linebreak because the opening
303: 		// delimiter is on its own line and is not included in the
304: 		// token Text itself, and the trailing newline is removed.
305: 		lineBreaks += 2
306: 	}
307: 	return lineBreaks
308: }
309: 
310: var heredocMarkerRegexp = regexp.MustCompile("^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$")
311: 
312: // isNextOnNewLine tests whether t2 is on a different line from t1
313: func isNextOnNewLine(t1, t2 Token) bool {
314: 	// If the second token is from a different file,
315: 	// we can assume it's from a different line
316: 	if t1.File != t2.File {
317: 		return true
318: 	}
319: 
320: 	// If the second token is from a different import chain,
321: 	// we can assume it's from a different line
322: 	if len(t1.imports) != len(t2.imports) {
323: 		return true
324: 	}
325: 	for i, im := range t1.imports {
326: 		if im != t2.imports[i] {
327: 			return true
328: 		}
329: 	}
330: 
331: 	// If the first token (incl line breaks) ends
332: 	// on a line earlier than the next token,
333: 	// then the second token is on a new line
334: 	return t1.Line+t1.NumLineBreaks() < t2.Line
335: }

part.text:
Implemented the heredoc parsing fix in `caddyconfig/caddyfile/lexer.go:138`.

Heredoc syntax is now only recognized when a valid marker immediately follows `<<`; otherwise tokens like `<<` and `>>` are lexed normally. Quoted `<<` is also handled correctly, while existing heredoc errors still work.

Validated with:

```sh
go test -count=1 ./caddyconfig/caddyfile/
```
